      Girls’ water polo captures narrow 11-10 victory against rival San Mateo

      Claire Hwang, Copy Editor • October 27, 2026
      Claire Hwang
      Junior and co-captain Ari Beser lunges for possession of the ball while fending off a San Mateo defender.

      By narrowly defeating San Mateo High School 11-10 on Thursday, Oct. 22, girls’ water polo (12-1) knocked San Mateo out of a three-way tie for the Peninsula Athletic League (PAL) Ocean Division crown, leaving themselves and Mercy High School tied for first place.

      Competing at an away game, the Panthers prepared in advance for San Mateo’s narrow pool and gameplay tactics.

      “The pool is very different because it’s a lot more narrow, so we tried to prepare in that sense,” junior Julia Bowler said. “We also know they’re really grabby, so we developed ways to maneuver around that, like keeping our hips up.”

      Because the Panthers had only beaten the Bearcats by a single point earlier this season, head coach Tiffany Spohrer said the team went into the rematch unsure of the outcome.

      “We went in feeling confident in our skills, but not confident that we could win. We went in knowing that either team could take the lead at any point in time,” Spohrer said.

      Despite the uncertainty, Burlingame took early control with a 7-4 lead by halftime and pulled away to 11-5 by the end of the third quarter.

      “In the third quarter, [San Mateo] only scored one goal and we scored many goals, so that was when it started feeling ‘Okay, we can definitely win this,’” senior and goalie Lucy Kendall said.

      • After the first quarter, the Panthers regrouped to sharpen their strategies and ended with a team cheer.

        Claire Hwang

      • After the hard-fought win, players circled up for the post-game team huddle.

        Claire Hwang

      • Senior and goalie Lucy Kendall scans the pool to find an open teammate to throw the ball to. Kendall blocked six goals in the first and third quarters of the game as goalie.

        Claire Hwang

      • Called up from junior varsity for this game, sophomore Kaila Johnstone was utilized for her speed.

        Claire Hwang

      • Freshman Kate Williams made significant contributions to the Panthers’ win with four goals and nine steals. With eight years of experience, she originally played club at Burlingame Aquatic Club before transitioning to Stanford Water Polo Club in seventh grade, where she continues to play in the off-season.

        Claire Hwang

      • Junior Leia Burlingham rises high out of the water to shoot the ball. Burlingham started every quarter, delivering an impressive three goals and three assists.

        Claire Hwang

      However, the comfortable lead fell apart in the fourth quarter as San Mateo surged forward with five continuous goals while Burlingame struggled to maintain their offense. As Kendall watched on the bench in the fourth quarter, she said she saw repeated one-on-nobodies occur.

      “I mostly watch the goalie because I’m a goalie, and the worst possible situation you can imagine as a goalie [occurred]. It’s what’s called a one-on-nobody, which is when the only thing in between the ball and the goal is you,” Kendall said. “There’s no defender, and that happened three or four times in that last quarter.”

      Although San Mateo narrowed the gap to 11-10 with 40 seconds left, Burlingame was able to successfully run out the clock to secure the win.

      Standout freshman Kate Williams, who led the team with four goals and nine steals, highlighted the high number of exclusion fouls – a foul resulting in a temporary exclusion from active play – the Panthers forced.

      “Some highlights were the amount of kickouts we got. I was really proud of our team for that,” Williams said. “A highlight for me was that I got two backhand [goals]. It’s a first for me.”

      The high-stakes atmosphere fueled aggressive play, leading to exclusion fouls on both sides. With this in mind, Spohrer said she hopes the players will work on remaining composed in intense situations.

      “The teams were playing really aggressively, and that’s not a fun game to play, but I am thankful that the refs were calling [fouls] on both sides,” Spohrer said. “I want the team to work on keeping their cool under pressure. Sometimes we can get really flustered when the other team is aggressive or when the score is really neck-and-neck, so I want them to keep their cool and stay clean in their own play.”

      The Panthers’ next game is on Tuesday, Oct. 27 against Mercy High School — the only team in their league they lost to this season — which will determine the PAL Ocean Division champion and advancement to the Central Coast Section playoffs.
